tldr_label: TL;DR — Israel votes amid reports Netanyahu sought a pre-election Iran strike; Brazil's markets crash

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Israelis vote today with early turnout the highest in decades, as Haaretz and Israeli TV report the IDF chief resisted Netanyahu's push for a pre-election strike on Iran; the government denies it. [[TAG:warning:contested reports]]

tldr_bullets.label: Brazil
tldr_bullets.body: The Ibovespa plunged 13.88%, its worst day since March 2020, and the dollar jumped 8.79% against the real after Lula's win; Flávio Bolsonaro dropped his bid to annul the vote. [[TAG:danger:Ibovespa -13.9%]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Trump called a ceasefire 'sort of a waste of time' and said the war will end soon; Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan agreed in Tehran to keep talking.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: US stocks rose Monday after Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq IPO; Asia rallied Tuesday and Brent eased toward $115 ahead of a Fed decision Wednesday.

tldr_bullets.label: Serbia
tldr_bullets.body: Aleksandar Vučić conceded after the student-led Student List won about 52.5% in parliamentary elections, ending his 14-year rule.

tldr_bullets.label: Egypt
tldr_bullets.body: Egypt's parliament authorized military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, reportedly air defenses and aircraft but no ground troops.

sections.title: Israel Votes
sections.summary: High turnout as reports say the IDF chief resisted Netanyahu's push for a pre-vote Iran strike

paragraphs.heading: Polls open
paragraphs.body: Turnout reached 16.68% by 10 a.m., the highest at that hour in decades, the Central Elections Committee said, according to Ynet and NBC News. About 7.3 million Israelis are eligible to vote and 36 parties are competing. Ynet said 600,000 to 650,000 special ballots from soldiers and displaced residents could delay final results until Thursday. [[TAG:info:results Thursday]]

paragraphs.heading: Strike controversy
paragraphs.body: Haaretz reported that senior Mossad officials opposed a pre-election Iran operation pushed by Netanyahu and backed by Mossad chief Roman Gofman, and Channel 12 reported that IDF chief Eyal Zamir resisted. CNN, via Haaretz, said Zamir warned his US counterpart a strike would disrupt the election and that Washington turned down Netanyahu's requests for joint attacks. Defense Minister Israel Katz called the reports 'completely baseless'. The claims rest on anonymous sources. [[TAG:danger:denied by government]]

sections.sources: Ynet, NBC News, CNN, Haaretz, Times of Israel, Mediaite

sections.title: Brazil: Markets Crash After Lula Win
sections.summary: Ibovespa falls 13.88% and the real slumps; Bolsonaro drops annulment bid for an abuse-of-power suit

paragraphs.heading: Historic sell-off
paragraphs.body: Brazil's Ibovespa fell 13.88% to 176,608, its steepest drop since March 2020, after a 10% slide triggered a 30-minute circuit breaker, The Rio Times and Nikkei Asia reported. The dollar rose 8.79% to 5.4154 reais, and long-dated dollar bonds fell. Lenders led losses while exporter Vale rose 4%. Investors had expected a Bolsonaro government to rein in spending, Al Jazeera reported. [[TAG:danger:circuit breaker]]

paragraphs.heading: Bolsonaro shifts course
paragraphs.body: Flávio Bolsonaro dropped his bid to annul the runoff and will instead file a case accusing Lula of abuse of power, Bloomberg reported, citing his campaign. His Liberal Party said it accepts the certified result, and the electoral court's president expressed 'absolute confidence' in the process, TRT World reported. Trump said 'I'm not running Brazil'. [[TAG:info:result accepted]]

sections.title: Iran War
sections.summary: Trump calls ceasefire 'a waste of time'; Tehran says US 'not serious'; regional talks to continue

paragraphs.heading: Trump's view
paragraphs.body: Trump said a ceasefire with Iran is 'sort of a waste of time', touting the US naval blockade as giving Washington 'total control' and saying the war will end soon, Iran International and Samaa reported. Tehran said the US is 'not serious' about talks, Al Jazeera reported. An Iranian lawmaker called for leaving the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. [[TAG:warning:hardening rhetoric]]

paragraphs.heading: Tehran talks
paragraphs.body: Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan agreed to continue security consultations after a meeting hosted by Mohsen Rezaei with Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, The New Arab and IranWire reported. No new security agreement or ceasefire was announced. A Pakistani official told Reuters the goal is a regional mechanism to prevent attacks. [[TAG:info:talks continue]]

paragraphs.heading: Gulf incidents
paragraphs.body: UKMTO reported a vessel on fire about 63 nautical miles southeast of Al-Faw, Iraq, classifying it as suspicious; the cause was not given, Maritime Executive and Kurdistan24 reported. Pezeshkian met Qatar's emir in Moscow at a gas forum, Khaleej Times reported.

sections.title: Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Egypt
sections.summary: Egypt authorizes defensive support for Saudi Arabia; 86% of Riyadh flights cancelled since Oct 8

paragraphs.heading: Egypt steps in
paragraphs.body: Egypt's parliament authorized President Sisi to provide military support to Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requests it, with at least two-thirds backing, the Washington Times and The Jerusalem Post reported. An unnamed regional official said it would involve air defenses and aircraft but no ground troops in Yemen. [[TAG:warning:Egypt joins]]

paragraphs.heading: Attacks and toll
paragraphs.body: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh and destroyed Houthi missile tunnels and launchers in Yemen, Al Jazeera reported; the Houthis claimed hits on East-West pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh's airport, which Saudi Arabia did not confirm. About 86% of scheduled flights at Riyadh's airport were cancelled between October 8 and 25, US News reported, and Bloomberg said the attacks have effectively shut Riyadh's financial district. [[TAG:danger:86% flights cut]]

sections.title: Markets
sections.summary: Anthropic IPO filing lifts tech; Kospi jumps 3.1%; Brent eases toward $115 before the Fed

paragraphs.heading: Monday's close
paragraphs.body: The S&P 500 rose 0.70% to 7,676.77, the Nasdaq 0.82% to 26,169.38 and the Dow 0.28% to 52,361.58, TheStreet reported, as Anthropic's IPO filing lifted sentiment and semiconductor stocks rallied about 3%. Verizon fell 3.2% after earnings. [[TAG:success:tech rebound]]

paragraphs.heading: Anthropic filing
paragraphs.body: Anthropic publicly filed for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker 'ANT', the company said; its S-1 does not yet set share count or price. Yahoo Finance and CNBC reported the filing shows $16.3 billion in first-half revenue. Reports point to a November listing. [[TAG:info:IPO filed]]

paragraphs.heading: Asia and oil
paragraphs.body: South Korea's Kospi closed up 3.1% at 5,638.34 and Japan's Nikkei rose as much as 2.2%, while Hong Kong and Shanghai slipped, the AP reported. Brent eased to about $114–$115 a barrel on hopes of US-Iran de-escalation, Voice of the Emirates and FXEmpire reported. The Fed decides Wednesday, and China's Communist Party is holding a closed-door plenum through Thursday.

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Zelensky says trilateral talks set for next month; Oleshky ceasefire begins; Kyiv hit again

paragraphs.heading: Talks and truce
paragraphs.body: Zelensky said Ukraine, Russia and the US have agreed to hold trilateral talks next month and again pressed for a meeting with Putin, Al Jazeera reported. Ukraine's General Staff said the local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky starts October 27 to allow civilian evacuations, according to Ukrainian Women's Guard. [[TAG:info:Oleshky truce]]

paragraphs.heading: Fighting
paragraphs.body: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv late on October 26, injuring five people including paramedics, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, and Ukraine's General Staff reported 185 combat engagements. Ukrainian forces struck military factories in Lipetsk, Oryol and Samara regions, 112.ua reported.

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump rallies in Mississippi and offers $1 million for voter-fraud tips; ballot disputes mount

paragraphs.heading: Campaign trail
paragraphs.body: Trump rallied in Corinth, Mississippi, for Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and said he would offer $1 million to anyone who reports voter fraud, NBC News reported. Vice President JD Vance campaigned in Montana and Kansas. Fox News reported Trump intensified attacks on Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed. [[TAG:info:8 days out]]

paragraphs.heading: Ballot fights
paragraphs.body: The Justice Department asked Washington state to set aside about 400 ballots it says may have been cast by noncitizens, and legal fights over disputed ballots in California and Alaska are raising questions about election administration, Fox News reported.

sections.title: Europe and Africa
sections.summary: Serbia's Vučić concedes to Student List; Nigeria's Ebola patient flown to Switzerland

paragraphs.heading: Serbia
paragraphs.body: Aleksandar Vučić conceded after the student movement's Student List won about 52.5% of the vote to 39.3% for his United Serbia list, with most polling stations counted, Euronews and NPR reported, ending his 14-year rule. The list has not named a prime ministerial candidate, Al Jazeera reported. [[TAG:success:power shift]]

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: Nigeria's first Ebola patient was evacuated to Switzerland, leaving Nigeria with no current cases, and Uganda tightened travel controls, CNN and Euronews reported. Africa CDC said scientists will investigate how she was infected; sequencing found her virus closely related to Kenyan patients' samples. Africa CDC's Ebola summit is set for October 28. [[TAG:warning:origin probe]]

paragraphs.heading: Elsewhere
paragraphs.body: Defense ministers from France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK met in Paris on Ukraine and Middle East security, and Cyprus signed a $1.8 billion deal to develop its first gas field, The Rio Times reported.

sections.sources: Euronews, NPR, Al Jazeera, CNN, US News, The Rio Times
